newsitem.title: GERMANY: German grain buyers cut new crop bid prices - ZMP.
newsitem.headline: German grain buyers cut new crop bid prices - ZMP.

text.p: German consumers of feed grains, bread rye and bread wheat have lowered bidding prices for the new crop by 10-30 marks a tonne from 1996 levels, the farm price and marketing office ZMP said in a market comment.
ZMP cited high stocks and looming harvest pressure.
Germany may repeat last year's record 42 million tonne grain crop in 1997 if a five percent area increase to 7.04 million hectares offsets yield losses as a result of a cool spring, it said.
ZMP said although domestic use of wheat, barley and maize had risen in the 1996/97 (July/June) campaign, consumers still had large stocks and were in no hurry to buy new crop.
German wheat from the old crop in June cost six percent less than last August while in France it was three percent lower and in Britain 13.5 percent lower.
Standard old crop bread wheat costs 270-280 marks fob in the spot market compared with 290-320 marks a year ago.
Another negative factor for German prices was import pressure from other EU countries, ZMP said.
It noted little grain had gone into intervention elsewhere, while at the last count Germany held roughly 90 percent of EU public grain stocks of around 1.8 million tonnes.
ZMP, which as a semi-official institution attempts to take a neutral line between producer and consumer interests, said sellers were hopeful the EU would resume subsidised grain exports.
They were hoping this could help stem further price declines in the run-up to harvesting.
Sellers were also happy that the EU had kept the cereals intervention price for the 1997/98 marketing year stable at its June 25 farm council.
The EU cut monthly storage payments but left the July/October intervention price at 119.19 Ecus/tonne, which at the July 1 Ecu/marks rate equalled 233.53 marks per tonne.
